General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

How Nintendo Recovered After Stumbling In The Streetpass

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By the time Nintendo ceased production of the 3DS in September 2020, the tech giant’s last dedicated line of exclusively handheld video game devices had completed one of gaming’s most incredible comebacks.
  • Industry observers note that the move worked: In its first month at its upcoming price, 3DS sales in America rose 260 percent.
  • One obvious issue with the launch was the games – or lack thereof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By the time Nintendo ceased production of the 3DS in September 2020, the tech giant’s last dedicated line of exclusively handheld video game devices had completed one of gaming’s most incredible comebacks. But to come back, you must first fall, and fall the 3DS did soon after it first launched in February 2011: its first month-and-a-half sales numbers came in nearly 400,000 units short of Nintendo’s initial projections of 4 million units sold. Over the next three months, Nintendo sold just an additional 710,000 3DS units worldwide, with only 110,000 purchased in the United States. In response, Nintendo took drastic measures, slashing the 3DS price in America from $250 to $170 just a half-year after the handheld launched.

Industry observers note that the move worked: In its first month at its upcoming price, 3DS sales in America rose 260 percent. According to metrics released by Nintendo last year, the 3DS family of devices ended its run at a stunning 76 million units sold, still half of the original DS’s total but far more than other Nintendo platforms like the GameCube (21.7 million), Nintendo 64 (32.9 million), SNES (49.1 million), and even the original NES (61.9 million). The little system that couldn’t eventually proved it could.

One obvious issue with the launch was the games – or lack thereof. Included in the modest North American 3DS launch lineup were just three Nintendo first-party titles: Nintendogs + Cats, Pilotwings Resort, and Steel Diver. Though a Zelda remake, a latest Mario platformer, and a new Mario Kart would arrive by year’s end, traditional system-selling franchises were initially nowhere to be found. By the time the bigger games arrived, Nintendo’s three first-party launch titles were placed in the dustbin of history, something Game Informer predicted in its review of Steel Diver, which labeled the game as “destined to become a strange and forgotten footnote in the publisher’s history.”.

According to recent reports, every first-party launch title communicates, both intentionally and unintentionally, something about the system upon which it’s launching and the manufacturer that created it. Last year, for instance, Mario Kart World evidenced that seamless open-world design and an interest in making buckets of money would remain hallmarks of Nintendo’s Switch 2 era. So, what can these three largely forgotten launch games tell us about the 3DS and Nintendo more broadly?

Initial hardware reviews of the 3DS contained two recurring thoughts: The glasses-free 3D effect was impressive when it worked – but it didn’t always work. Engadget’s review further hypothesized that “a lot of people are going to buy a 3DS and find they don’t really care for the 3D effect.” By the time Super Mario 3D Land released nine months after launch, Game Informer’s Bryan Vore was startled to find he was using the system’s primary feature at all, writing, “What surprises me most about 3D Land is how well the 3D effect is handled. I kept the 3D slider up most of the game”.

It has been revealed that indeed, in Nintendo’s 2011 fiscal year report, president Satoru Iwata theorized that initial 3DS sales were underwhelming because the tech giant had not done a convincing enough job of explaining the system’s signature innovation to potential customers: “The value of 3D images without the need for special glasses is hard to be understood through the existing media. However, we have found that people cannot feel it just by trying out a device, rather, some might even misestimate it when experiencing the images in an improper fashion.” Just two and a half years after the system’s launch, Nintendo began selling a fully flattened version of the handheld, appropriately named the 2DS.

Recent findings suggest that part of the concern with the underwhelming launch was that the 3DS lineup lacked an obvious killer app: There was neither a clear game that made purchasing the handheld an easy decision, nor was there a game that immediately proved that the 3D effect was anything more than an optional gimmick. In fact, among the three first-party titles was a game that had been designed nearly to completion before the team even learned of the existence of the 3DS.

When Nintendo first began showing the original DS to journalists at E3 in 2004, included among upcoming releases, like Metroid Prime Hunters and WarioWare Touched!, was a humble submarine simulation tech demo. IGN’s hands-on preview called the sub demo “simple in concept, but surprisingly complex in its controls and gameplay,” noting that it was “one of those ‘fun, but not quite a full game’ games at Nintendo’s booth, so it’s hard to say if development teams will expand on Submarine’s design to make it a more complete package.” At first, the team that made the demo, comprising veterans from Star Fox and F-Zero, was also unsure if they would expand it into a full game, as many of its members began work on other projects like Wii Fit.

According to recent reports, much later, producer Tadashi Sugiyama said in an Iwata Asks interview posted on Nintendo’s website that Nintendo of America asked the team to reconvene and release the submarine demo as downloadable software for the Nintendo DSi. But as the game – soon to be titled Steel Diver – expanded from just one mode (the side-scrolling submarine exploration and combat that would form the bulk of the game’s missions) to three modes (including Periscope Strike, a first-person torpedo shooter from the perspective of a periscope, and Steel Commander, a top-down strategy game partially inspired by the Japanese-exclusive 1990 Game Boy game Kaisen Game: Radar Mission), the Steel Diver team – now composed of both Nintendo designers and the 11 members of Giles Goddard’s firm Vitei – decided to expand their demo into a full retail release. This initially led to an identity crisis for director Takaya Imamura, who revealed to Iwata that he briefly, “thought it would be fine to set the game in a flashy, glittery world like – and I’m not kidding – a submarine version of Mario Kart.” Sugiyama promptly shut that idea down, and the game proceeded with more traditional aquatic environments.

According to recent reports, highly invested in the project was the legendary Shigeru Miyamoto, who held a key piece of information from the team: Though Steel Diver was developed for the DS, he thought that it would make an even better showcase for the company’s yet-to-be-revealed 3DS. But it wasn’t until very late into the development process that the Steel Diver team even learned of the existence of the latest console, a decision Miyamoto explained in Iwata Asks: “I knew the game was perfect for the Nintendo 3DS system, but I was afraid that if we switched from the Nintendo DS system to the Nintendo 3DS system in the middle of development, the contents wouldn’t be thoroughly fine-tuned. So after the Nintendo DS version was about done, I said, ‘Let’s shift this over to the Nintendo 3DS system.’” According to Imamura, “[w]hen we heard that, we already had intends for debugging. Development was all but over.”.

According to recent reports, the process of adding an extra dimension to the game proved difficult at first, with Imamura telling Iwata, “We thought we could just switch it over and it would look stereoscopic, but when we did, we couldn’t see it. […] We were among the first to develop software for the Nintendo 3DS system, so a sufficient development kit didn’t exist at the time.” But then, “one day it suddenly started popping out,” Goddard remarked in that same Iwata Asks article. And it came at just the right time, Goddard added: “It started looking 3D about the day before our presentation. If it hadn’t, the whole thing might have ended.” Ultimately, Imamura felt that the game had found its correct home on the 3DS, even if the process could have been improved: “I’m really glad we changed it over to the Nintendo 3DS system. But I think it would have turned out even better if Miyamoto-san had told us sooner that he wanted to make it for the Nintendo 3DS system [laughs]!”.

Industry observers note that when the Wii released in 2006, it came bundled with a number of pre-installed “channels” – or what we would likely just call apps today. Among those was the Mii Channel, an avatar-maker co-directed by Animal Crossing and Splatoon creator Hisashi Nogami. In an Iwata Asks interview, Nogami said that something like the Miis was an idea Miyamoto “had wanted to realize for some time.” Nogami revealed that originally the “plan was to develop three games in which the same characters designed by the player would appear.” But as development on the Wii advanced, the concept had “broadened to encompass the entire Wii.” Miis were integral features of the Wii’s user-interface, appearing in a large number of games including, most importantly, the Wii’s landmark pack-in, Wii Sports, and becoming a defining aspect of Nintendo’s cultural identity. In a 2008 fiscal report Q&A, Iwata made clear just how seriously the organization viewed Miis as part of its brand, stating that, to “Nintendo, licensing Mii is identical to licensing Mario.” The Mii was now Nintendo, and it should be treated like its other icons.

It has been revealed that however, it was not immediately clear to the general public whether the Mii was tied specifically to the Wii – with which it shared all but one letter – or if it would become Nintendo’s default avatar-creation system for the next two decades-plus, as we now know it has. Having launched in 2004, the DS did not include native Mii creation software, but it showed the first small signs that the Mii would become a core part of the larger Nintendo ecosystem.

First, the thrillingly titled DS exercise game Personal Trainer: Walking – released in 2008 in Japan and 2009 in America – tied players’ pedometer-tracked steps to Mii avatars, which could be imported over from the Wii’s Mii Channel. However, players who did not own a Wii could only choose Miis from a series of random presets; there was no way to create a custom Mii within the game itself. The first DS game to feature a full Mii creation suite was 2009’s Tomodachi Collection, a Japan-exclusive social simulation game that would receive a more widely released sequel on the 3DS in 2013/2014 (a third game will arrive later this year.) But only three other DS games featured Miis at all: Ide Yousuke’s Healthy Mahjong DSi, a Japan-exclusive downloadable mahjong game; Kuruma de DS, also exclusive to Japan, a GPS-connected title made in collaboration with Toyota and Honda that could only be used in select cars; and Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time, which could feature a Mii-emblazoned item only if the player was connected to someone playing on a Wii.

In a recent development, it wasn’t until the 3DS that it became clear that Miis would truly migrate away from their home system. The 3DS was pre-installed with an avatar creation application called Mii Maker. One of the system’s novel features was “StreetPass,” a communication system that allowed players to exchange data with other nearby players. Its showcase app was StreetPass Mii Plaza, in which up to 10 Miis could congregate and compete in minigames. By the end of 2013, the 3DS even had its own version of Miiverse, the Mii-based social network that first appeared on the Wii U.

Recent findings suggest that the surest sign that Miis were here for good was Pilotwings Resort. The 3DS launch title was the third – and final, for now – entry in the Miyamoto-created Pilotwings franchise of flight-simulation games. Each of the previous games had also served as North American launch titles for their respective systems, with each game functioning as a technical showcase for its system’s upgraded graphical capabilities. 1991’s Pilotwings utilized the Super Nintendo’s Mode 7 graphics to deliver groundbreaking “3D” visuals, while 1996’s Pilotwings 64 gave players the chance to explore the Nintendo 64’s more authentically three-dimensional spaces. Pilotwings Resort continued this trend, affording early 3DS adopters a massive playground to experiment with the system’s stereoscopic 3D visuals.

The earlier Pilotwings were not full of classic Nintendo iconography, but Pilotwings Resort represented a major aesthetic break: Every character in the game was a Mii. This aligned the game more closely with a different recent – and more recognizable – Nintendo series: Wii Sports. The action of Pilotwings Resort even takes place on Wuhu Island, the fictional tropical location where 2007’s Wii Fit and 2009’s Wii Sports Resort were also set.

The origins of the island, however, trace back even further. When Nintendo showcased the Wii to journalists in May 2006, Wii Sports contained an additional game that was cut from the final release: a flight simulator called Airplane, in which players soared above an unnamed island that bore a number of striking similarities to Wuhu. Interestingly, as detailed in a 2006 Eurogamer article, Nintendo reps were quick to downplay any connection between Wii Sports Airplane and the Pilotwings franchise, with Matthew Kumar writing, “It’s not a Pilotwings, they say, despite featuring a lovely, relaxing island which features small towns to buzz over, and tunnels to barnstorm. And, oh, you know, rings to fly through to get points.” Additionally, Kumar wrote, “It’s not entirely clear how this would fit into the Wii Sports range (or pack) or, despite what they say, if it is even intended to. But as a tech demo for that Pilotwings game they’re going to unveil at TGS or something, it’s brilliant and I’m gasping for more.” By the time Pilotwings Resort finally saw the light of day a half-decade later, the Wii Sports franchise – and its iconic Miis – had climbed so high up the hierarchy of Nintendo’s first-party franchises that IGN’s review of the game opened with, “Wii Sports Resort is back. Did you miss it?”.

Industry observers note that miis appeared throughout the 3DS’s lifetime. They served as player icons for games like Super Mario 3D Land and Kid Icarus: Uprising, even starring in their own idiosyncratic games like Tomodachi Life and Miitopia. Miis would also be baked into future systems like the Wii U, the Switch, and the Switch 2. But it was Pilotwings Resort – along with Mii Plaza – that demonstrated Nintendo had bigger and more serious aspirations for the Mii outside of the Wii.

When the original Game Boy rolled out in 1989, arriving in tow was an accessory called the Game Link Cable. It allowed players to connect directly to other Game Boy systems, enabling competitive multiplayer sessions in early hits like Tetris. Seven years later, with the release of the first Pokémon games, the Game Link Cable found a fresh calling, allowing players to not just compete, but also to swap their pocket monsters with other players in their communities. In her book Super Nintendo: How One Japanese Company Helped the World Have Fun, Keza MacDonald argues that this marked a turning point for Nintendo: “Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue’s emphasis on trading and sharing represented an inspired reinvention of the Game Boy Link Cable: Game Freak took a piece of technology that had been used exclusively for competition and made it about communication, as well.”.

It has been revealed that that design principle – that games were about sharing and communication, too – reached its apotheosis with the 3DS’s StreetPass feature, which allowed the system to actively and, more interestingly, passively communicate with other nearby 3DSs via locally established, internet-free connections, even when the console was set to sleep mode. At launch, StreetPass was most prominently featured in the preinstalled Mii StreetPass Plaza app, which included the game Find Mii, an RPG in which players’ parties were filled with Miis taken from other 3DSs they had passed by. As producer Kouichi Kawamoto told Kotaku’s Stephen Totilo, Find Mii emerged “from our drive to make players feel like they accomplish something by using StreetPass”. It was an idle game powered by physical activity. In doing so, StreetPass’s communication had taken the sharing principles of the Game Link Cable in an entirely novel direction.

StreetPass was also implemented into Nintendogs + Cats, the best-selling of the 3DS’s first-party launch titles. While Pokémon players of yore had to establish a physical connection to see other players’ collections, StreetPass enabled Nintendogs players to passively interact with other owners and their pets. You could take your 3DS on a walk to an actual dog park, for example, and if there were any other 3DS owners in range, you would head home with a series of journal entries featuring their Miis, their pets, any messages they’d sent, and perhaps even a gift. These Miis and their pets would also soon begin to populate the game in other ways: You might run into them on a walk or even compete against them in dog shows. Nintendogs on DS featured a similar feature – Bark Mode – but it required more active participation from players; with StreetPass, community-building was now a low-effort exercise (often involving actual exercise).

According to recent reports, streetPass was central to Nintendo’s conception of the 3DS. In an Iwata Asks article, the eponymous Iwata said that the concept of the 3DS was, “Carry Around, Affect Each Other and Something Upcoming Every Day.” Nintendogs + Cats producer Hideki Konno further stated, “[W]hile it’s definitely okay to enjoy the game at home, I hope players will go out walking around with their Nintendo 3DS system as often as possible. There’s a lot for that purpose not just in Nintendogs + Cats, but built into the system itself”. StreetPass was exactly the kind of kooky invention upon which Nintendo made its name, and its legacy of encouraging players to explore the world lives on in mobile games like Pokémon Go.

The 3DS would soon find better games – and better sales – but its modest launch lineup contained plenty of insight. Steel Diver’s winding path towards release evidenced Nintendo’s unwavering commitment to its internal ideas – and its most legendary designer’s unconventional style of communication. Pilotwings Resort further established a core part of Nintendo’s brand identity, while Nintendogs + Cats showed that even the most straightforward of Nintendo sequels could still feature peculiar innovations. Stereoscopic 3D may not have been the future of gaming, but other elements of the 3DS have stayed with us forever.

Feature: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score.
  • According to recent reports, both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur.
  • According to recent reports, we've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score. But just because we gave it a 10/10 here at Pure Xbox doesn't mean there isn't still some wiggle room for improvement.

According to recent reports, both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur. However, we've also noticed a few things we'd like to see fixed or added to GTA VI to make it even better. Think of this article like adding marshmallows to a hot chocolate: we're looking to take something great and make it even sweeter.

According to recent reports, we've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI. Let's get into it:.

Recent findings suggest that you've all noticed the darkness that appears from time to time around the screen, right? That's a vignette and GTA VI is a significant fan of them. It's most noticeable when you're booking it down the North 97 highway or, in the worst-case scenario, flying over the Keys as shown in the above screenshot.

It has been revealed that GTA VI uses vignettes to cleverly draw your focus to the most important parts of the screen. I honestly think it's a great technique for making things feel more cinematic. Although, it is quite pants that there's no option to reduce its intensity or turn it off altogether. If Rockstar could give us the ability to toggle the vignette on and off, that would be great, because it also seems to be one of the most requested changes amongst GTA VI players.

In a recent development, something I've grown increasingly aware of is the inability to wait or sleep to pass time across Leonida. I was particularly irked after an 18-hole crazy golf competition against Jason saw the sun set on us, and I didn't fancy driving all the way back to my lodging in Vice City. I wanted to pass time in my car or a nearby eatery, but my only option appeared to be the 4-5 minute drive home - made worse knowing that once morning hit, I'd just want to do the drive back and play golf in the daylight.

Industry observers note that it's probably the fault of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its extremely handy wilderness camps. They were great in a pinch to let you pass time quickly. What would be great is if GTA VI gave players the option to rough it in their car for the night or find a nearby hotel room or something.

Sources indicate that I was on a mission to pick up some prescription drugs when my car was escorted slowly into an enemy compound and the camera suddenly switched from third-person to first-person. Seeing Lucia's impeccable nails gripped around the steering wheel made me realise there's no legitimate way to drive from a behind-the-wheel perspective.

Sure, there's that glitch that lets you play GTA VI in first-person, but it would be better if Rockstar implemented an additional first-person POV for driving.

It seems like a bit of a no-brainer, but we'd love to see AMD FSR 4.1 implementation on Xbox Series X. GTA VI is already up-and-running with FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S which brings internal resolutions up from 720p to 1080p output. It's good going on XSS, but we'd like to see what it can do with XSX.

If a game rolls out with a good Photo Mode, then you may as well tack an extra 10 hours onto my playthrough. But GTA VI? Maybe add another 20-30 hours. It's gorgeous!

Recent findings suggest that the Photo Mode in this game is already solid. You can set up light sources, adjust focus and aperture, and as a graduate photographer, I think it's all rather intuitive. There's even a selfie mode where players can pose Jason and Lucia together, adjust their facial expressions and change their poses.

What I'd like to see is that same flexibility expand beyond selfie mode. I'd like to be able to adjust the lovers to better match the photos I'm trying to create. It was during a tense getaway, four-stars and neck-deep in trouble, that I thought I'd take an action shot, only to find Jason had blinked and Lucia looked bored as hell. It would be great to have the option to adjust expressions, head directions, poses and all that sort of stuff.

Recent findings suggest that please fix the sliders when handling amounts of money, Rockstar. Please. It's not the biggest fix, nor the most elaborate, so I'll keep it brief.

In a recent development, whenever I open my phone to buck myself some cash, I often struggle to select the right amount rapidly. It takes too long for the slider to speed up as I increase the amount, but then it very quickly gets out of control, and I end up overshooting my intended figure. Plus, the sound it makes is quite horrid.

What would help is having set increments to scroll through, say, $1, $10, $50, $100 and so on. It might just smooth out the experience a smidge.

Sources indicate that I'd like to wrap up with a quickfire segment of some of our own suggestions on how Rockstar could improve GTA VI, but also some of yours. So, let's get through it.

Sources indicate that I'd love to be able to call NPC buddies like Cal for a round of crazy golf. At the moment, playing with a partner is limited to Jason and Lucia. I'm all for love, but sometimes you need some friendly bonding too.

It has been revealed that another one I'd personally like to see is custom music stations on in-game radios. Now, I know this isn't something likely to happen, but it would be cool to link my Spotify and Rockstar accounts to play my own curated playlists.

Oh, and for the love of all things matrimony, please let me make a coffee for Jason/Lucia and actually give it to them. I've experienced Jason asking for a cuppa joe, so let me do the do, y'know?

According to recent reports, something Fraser mentioned he'd like to see is additional minigames like bowling or darts added to the game. The developers said they ran out of time for things like this, so maybe they could add them as a post-launch enhancement.

And to wrap up, I've spotted folks online requesting the ability to dial any phone number like you could in previous games, as well as blind firing around cover during firefights, buying housing property, and having save states pick up directly where you left off.

Industry observers note that so, there you have it. Some of our suggestions and some we've found out in the wild, but we'd love to hear your ideas on what might make GTA VI a better game. Be sure to chat with us in the comments!

Love and Deepspace’s latest upgrade is here, adding a fresh Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

According to recent reports, the upcoming Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Recent findings suggest that alongside the big newly introduced Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the upcoming Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the upcoming revision. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re fresh to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an notable part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

It's shy of the 537,000 Link's latest put up in its debut week, of course, but for a box with no disc in it, it's not bad going.

The rest of the chart is a Switch-fest, mind you, with the likes of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and Rhythm Heaven Groove still performing well, and last week's silver medallist, Metaphor: ReFantazio, hanging in there at ninth.

Momotaro Dentetsu 2: Anata no Machi mo Kitto Aru – Higashi Nihon Hen + Nishi Nihon Hen.

  • Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's at the moment only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

Industry observers note that alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend. EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 introduced," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M.".

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

Recent findings suggest that during that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable.".

GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (441 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • "After the substantial day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the substantial day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It notes a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

In a recent development, uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are presently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

Sources indicate that as popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the tech giant has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain.
  • Industry observers note that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place".
  • "We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up newly introduced possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Industry observers note that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft declared at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up newly introduced possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot mentioned.

Sources indicate that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec mentioned. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing initiative with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

That'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the firm affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

In a recent development, it’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next massive test isn’t far off.

It has been revealed that hoYoverse confirmed today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that fresh faces will be available in this test is significant news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

According to recent reports, the Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As declared in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.
  • Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS.
  • Industry observers note that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As declared in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Industry observers note that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days.
  • The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal.
  • Sources indicate that the way you do so is relatively simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this upcoming pet.

Sources indicate that the way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the substantial deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

This is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

GTA 6's best lore drops happen when you're chilling with your partner, so stop leaving them at home all the time

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk.
  • Recent findings suggest that sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do.

And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.

But then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together.

Industry observers note that I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too.

Recent findings suggest that that doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother.

I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far.

#155126. GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (536 w)

GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • Industry observers note that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

Industry observers note that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying newly introduced," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

It has been revealed that though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

In a recent development, of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony looks to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Recent findings suggest that disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we right now consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

According to recent reports, using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

It has been revealed that last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

According to recent reports, I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

According to recent reports, this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

In a recent development, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major enhancement, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

Recent findings suggest that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The newly introduced update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

In a recent development, the big inciting incident of this fresh chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first fresh arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

It has been revealed that her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

It has been revealed that this is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent upcoming characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Industry observers note that evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a upcoming weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a substantial expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding upcoming decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 rolls out and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now.
  • Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me.
  • It has been revealed that xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

It has been revealed that xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

Industry observers note that one day, I fancied playing on the major screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I stated, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have plans to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer.".

According to Jez Corden, the original initiative for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

Back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

In a recent development, pure Xbox, we'd love to hear what you think about this. Make sure to vote in the poll below and tell us more in the comments section.

Breaking: Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (353 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

In order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any concerns and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand new arrival that the firm just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar concern recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

Review: Gamesir Nova Vision Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - Unique Features Elevate This Mid-Range Pad

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (961 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC.
  • The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools.
  • Sources indicate that the analogue sticks really are the star of the show.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC. So when it declared the new Nova Vision, my Spider-Sense tingled.

The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools. At $54.99, this is a compelling controller as it is, but Gamesir has also included a charging stand to ensure you’re always good to go.

Sources indicate that the analogue sticks really are the star of the show. Featuring raised, textured edges with a grippy rubber material, they actually share much in common with the PS5 analogue sticks and feel great to use. The Hall Effect technology should keep stick drift at bay, while the transparent domes let you see into the interior – a neat little touch I personally liked. My wife wasn’t keen on it, so your own appreciation may vary.

Adjustable tension isn’t completely new — Gulikit’s TT Pro and Max controllers do the same thing — but this is the first instance I’ve tried a controller that lets you do it without any extra tools. All you need to do is twist the sticks anti-clockwise to loosen the tension, and clockwise to tighten.

At their loosest, the sticks feel light and floaty, good for open-world games like Breath of the Wild in which you need to move great distances. At their tightest, they allow for more precise movements, which might come in handy for racing games like Mario Kart World or first-person shooters like Modern Warfare 4.

Had it required an extra tool to adjust the tension, I might have just left the Nova Vision at one setting and been done with it. However, being able to simply twist the sticks to my desired tension at any point encouraged experimentation based on the game I’m playing. It’s a neat feature, and thankfully they take a fair bit of pressure to twist, so you’re never going to do it accidentally.

Sources indicate that the screen acts as your main hub for functions and customisation. You might notice at first glance that the Vision is lacking buttons for Start, Select, and Home - they’re all housed in the screen. Click it on the bottom right for Start, the bottom left for Select, and anywhere near the top for Home.

Industry observers note that then you’ve got the ‘M’ button at the bottom, nestled in between the D-pad and right analogue stick. Hold this down for about five seconds to access the configuration menu. Here, you can select whether to connect to Switch, PC, or mobile, remap buttons to your liking, switch between profiles, adjust motion controls and vibration intensity, and more.

When you’re in the configuration menu, navigation is simple: use the D-pad to highlight menu items, ‘A’ to select, and ‘B’ to go back. When you’re done, just hold down the ‘M’ button again to exit. If you’re wondering where the capture button is, there isn’t one, but a quick double-tap of ‘M’ provides the same functionality. There’s no ‘C’ button for chat, mind you.

Inputs feel pretty good, overall. The D-pad, shoulder buttons, and back buttons are mechanical and provide a nice, satisfying click when pressed. The ABXY inputs, meanwhile, are membrane and considerably quieter by comparison. The main shoulder triggers can be swapped between full motion travel and short, clicky stops, so experiment with this to find your preference.

The back buttons aren’t mapped to anything by default. You can map any individual input to the buttons, or opt for any combo macro up to 12 inputs. They’re positioned nicely, allowing your middle fingers to rest comfortably, and they’re much quieter than some of the competition on the market.

Connection is done in three ways: Bluetooth, 2.4G wireless via a dongle, or a USB-C cable. The 1000mAh battery should comfortably last over 10 hours on a single charge, but if you’re using the included charging dock, you’ll likely never need to worry about this. The dock itself is pretty small and minimal in its design, with a nice, subtle RGB strip that slowly pulses when the controller is docked. And yes, it does feature wake-up support for Switch 2.

Industry observers note that finally, it’s worth mentioning that you can further customise the controller via the Gamesir Connect PC app, allowing you to add your own images and GIFs to the built-in screen. Unfortunately, the downside here is that it’s not compatible with Mac, so I’ve been unable to test this feature out myself.

For the mid-range price, the Nova Vision is an excellent controller for Switch 1 and 2. The built-in screen allows for quick customisation and remapping if needed, while the adjustable tension in the analogue sticks feels intuitive and genuinely useful for different games and genres. Add in Hall Effect technology and the charging dock, and you’re getting a lot of bang for your buck.

The lack of a ‘C’ button is a shame, while introducing Mac compatibility for the Gamesir Connect app would be an easy win. Furthermore, some folks just might not be keen on functions like Start and Home being accessed via the screen. If that’s you, then this probably isn’t for you. For everyone else, the Nova Vision is a solid choice.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • According to recent reports, the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

According to recent reports, the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

"It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson noted the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson said, adding that websites may return in the future.

"I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

Industry observers note that "We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," mentioned Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a substantial shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore new possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its major heart.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a newly introduced installment.
  • Industry observers note that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
  • What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a newly introduced installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

Industry observers note that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

It has been revealed that the game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

Recent findings suggest that 2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The fresh protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.
