📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

Industry observers note that the UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Sources indicate that either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

It has been revealed that cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Upcoming Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Special Presentation," which featured a newly introduced trailer for the expansion alongside the announcement of its release date (and the showcase of three lovely looking indie titles). And thankfully we're not going to be waiting very long, as Sea of Sorrow is coming out in two weeks, with the devs hyping it up as an "expansion unlike any we've done before.".

Sources indicate that as promised, Sea of Sorrow is a "high-seas adventure," with the trailer featuring Hornet arriving on a boat to uncharted shores and taking the fight to pirate bugs who yelp "arghhh" when you beat them with a very Donkey Kong Country 2-coded sound effect. We also saw her blasting out of cannons, climbing net ladders, and getting in scraps with multiple giant pirate bosses.

We knew its release had to be soon as the DLC, which was unveiled shortly after Silksong rolled out, was previously given a 2026 release window – although given the reveal to release timeline of the game itself, it's perhaps no surprise that some have not been so trusting, especially when that date vanished on the game's physical copy.

While Silksong famously started out as a DLC for the original Hollow Knight, it's easy to forget that the original got multiple DLC packs, with four free expansions released within its two years. Team Cherry didn't confirm what DLC is still to come for Silksong, but given it's the "first significant content update" I'm sure fans will be fed for a while yet.

Katana Zero pulls a Hollow Knight: Silksong - the beloved action game's DLC is now "the size of a full sequel" after 7 years of development.

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

In terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

It has been revealed that it was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

"GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days.".

Sources indicate that just last week, on the day of GTA 6's release, we mentioned how Xbox hardware spending in the U.S. was up 42% YoY in October, attributed to the likes of Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6.

It's going to be fascinating to see how the rest of the world stacks up in terms of Xbox sales data from November (which should be revealed over the coming days and weeks), and indeed whether GTA 6's physical edition is also setting records in even more regions. It most likely is - this is a ridiculously popular game after all.

According to recent reports, hoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a fresh chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The newly introduced narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Sources indicate that mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

Sources indicate that while the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

According to recent reports, you can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can proposal where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another newly introduced addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A fresh Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild.
  • In a recent development, in much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it.
  • In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-latest sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In a recent development, in much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise latest players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some issues where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

According to recent reports, the Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…".

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty quickly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one.".

Industry observers note that in general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon noted. "That's the level we were aiming for.".

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, claims it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure.".

Recent findings suggest that finCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.

Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X. "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music.".

A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization.".

Sources indicate that as Corcos writes in its readme, Legatum is "largely" built with the use of AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated. While FinCEN addresses its cybersecurity breach, Corcos and his Claude agents have been steadily pushing updates: At time of writing, the latest commit—added just six minutes ago—tweaked some of its AI art.

Among the other half-dozen or so commits in the last three hours are adjustments to map generation, music updates, and—let's see—attempts at stemming "a wave of political problems and README vandalism" left by Github owners.

That automated moderation evidently still needs some optimizing, judging from the repo's Glitch #220, which reads: "Lead developer is a giant asshole." Another issue notes that "late game American civilization feels broken," because "when you get the Large Language Model tech unlocked, it pretty much destroys any chance of a cultural victory because all your artists are gone, and all your government buildings become totally useless.".

FinCEN isn't the only US government organization suffering cybersecurity concerns this week. Yesterday, The New York Times reported that the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Security, and the Department of Defense's National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency had been impacted by a vulnerability in an open source intelligence system, which exposed unclassified information.

In a recent development, on X, Corcos has addressed the questionable optics of overseeing a vibecoded Civ knockoff while his department's facing a cybersecurity intrusion: "Just a heads up, the computers are doing it on their own," Corcos mentioned in a reply to a user who compared the incident to Nero fiddling while Rome burned. "Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops.".

Sources indicate that in another reply to a more sympathetic user, Corcos was more enthusiastic: "These tools are getting so good it's blowing my mind. A brief voice note on my phone can kick off an amount of work that would have taken dozens of people weeks to deliver," he stated. "So cool.".

In a recent development, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

It has been revealed that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

It has been revealed that "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

Recent findings suggest that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

Recent findings suggest that "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too.
  • Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching upcoming consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.
  • According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching upcoming consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching new consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,".

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed swiftly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

However, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

Recent findings suggest that "If data centre demand grows, then it could rapidly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand.".

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has noted a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a big push with a newly introduced console.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together. However, there was one huge event that didn't include David Schwimmer's character, and there's a specific reason why. While Ross's absence from this particular scene was unfortunate, it did lead to a clever joke and a nod to something the character had become notorious for.

Industry observers note that the end of Season 6 of Friends was a big one. Chandler had done too good a job throwing Monica off the scent of his planned proposal – so much so that it seemed like she was actually considering Richard's proposal of marriage and a family – and was frantic to correct the situation. The big twist came when he came rushing back to the apartment, being made to believe he was too late, only to find Monica waiting for him with a proposal of her own.

Sources indicate that monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them. The only person absent was Ross. No, David Schwimmer and Friends weren't "on a break," he was just busy overseas when the engagement scene was filmed.

Recent findings suggest that as Friends co-creator David Crane pointed out on the DVD commentary, all of David Schwimmer's scenes for the two-part Season 6 finale had to be filmed in the first week because the actor was in England filming Band of Brothers for HBO. Crane spoke about having to film the scene without Schwimmer, saying:.

In a recent development, it was frustrating not having him because you feel as though there's a major event on the show, Monica and Chandler are engaged, and all the friends run in, but not quite all the friends. The moment still works, and it's still moving, but it would have been nice to have him for that, but we were not prepared to film that scene the previous week.

While all of the drama between Monica and Chandler was going on throughout "The One with the Proposal," Ross was busy breaking up with college student Elizabeth (a cliffhanger involving her revealing she's pregnant was discussed for the season finale, but ultimately scrapped). From what it sounds like, that was all filmed during the first week of production for these final episodes. The grand finale involving Chandler and Monica wasn't filmed until later.

According to recent reports, as you'll recall, as the gang is celebrating with a group hug, Phoebe points out that "Ross isn't here!" to which Rachel responds, "Oh, hell, he's done this three times. He knows what it's about!" It's a funny way to acknowledge and then dismiss Ross's absence from his sister and best friend's engagement, while also firing a shot at Ross's "three-divorce guy" reputation. As Crane put it, that was the silver lining to the situation, after debating whether or not to point out the lack of Ross in the scene:.

There was a lot of debate. Do you need to acknowledge the fact that Ross isn't here? Or do you just let it go? And it actually gave us a really good joke.

I'll admit, the absence of a main character due to the actor being involved in another project might bother me under other circumstances, but it's hard to complain here. Band of Brothers is its own kind of epic, after all. Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks' HBO miniseries – based on Stephen Ambrose's non-fiction book about a parachute infantry firm serving in World War II – won several Emmys and has been widely remembered and appreciated in the decades since its release. What's more, Schwimmer's portrayal of Captain Herbert Sobel is easily one of his most memorable roles outside of the hit sitcom.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

The writers made the best of the situation by working in the joke about marriage proposals being old hat for Ross.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Ross did get in on the celebrations for Monica and Chandler, but it doesn't happen until the start of the following season. Ross learns about his sister and Chandler's engagement early in the Season 7 premiere, when he shows up at the apartment with a bottle of champagne and a candy bar that they requested him to bring.

You can watch Friends and Band of Brothers with an HBO Max subscription.

Kelly put her life-long love of movies, TV and books to greater use when she joined CinemaBlend as a freelance TV news writer in 2006, and went on to serve as the site’s TV Editor before joining the staff full-time in 2011 and moving over to other roles at the site. At present, she’s an Assistant Managing Editor who spends much of her time brainstorming and editing features, analyzing site data, working with writers and editors on content planning and the workflow, and obsessing over the best movies and TV highlights. She graduated from SUNY Cortland with BA in Communication Studies and a minor in Cinema Studies. When she isn't working, she's probably thinking about work, or reading (or listening to a book), and making sure her cats are living their absolute best feline lives.

Breaking: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet stated. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Recent findings suggest that ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

According to recent reports, ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the organization is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft claims the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active people over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

Industry observers note that the news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft confirmed in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

According to recent reports, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a latest Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's notable questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

Recent findings suggest that in this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

Sources indicate that you can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

In a recent development, the cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

It has been revealed that would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

#155053. Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2221 w)

Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.
  • It has been revealed that that's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy.
  • This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

It has been revealed that that's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

According to recent reports, if you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

For a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

Before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokiri Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

Visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

Head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

You'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

According to recent reports, after finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

When ready, head to Death Mountain.

According to recent reports, the aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Industry observers note that inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

Now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

According to recent reports, inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!).

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

Once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

According to recent reports, after the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

In a recent development, to leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

It has been revealed that complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Big Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

According to recent reports, on the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

In a recent development, head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

With both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.).

Recent findings suggest that when you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's currently blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

If you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

With that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two newly introduced items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

Sources indicate that the tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are announced and Xbox doesn't make a significant deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and new Fallout games where it felt like they were unveiled without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is revealed / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

It has been revealed that let's see what happens in the Fresh Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

Industry observers note that what are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

It has been revealed that motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames, but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series states "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "newly introduced AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred said. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole fresh set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.".

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.

Not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark.".

According to recent reports, "What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death.".

"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.

Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death.

"But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield said, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.

At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so.

"I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa said at the time.

The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon mentioned. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

Recent findings suggest that moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

According to recent reports, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Recent findings suggest that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

  • The BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence.
  • According to recent reports, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

The BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

According to recent reports, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

According to recent reports, kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

According to recent reports, 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

In a recent development, earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Industry observers note that cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

I mention this because latest, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

In a recent development, this risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

The plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

According to recent reports, as in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

According to recent reports, "Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

'The Results Are Very, Very Impressive' - Digital Foundry Praises GTA 6 On Xbox One

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • It has been revealed that xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

It has been revealed that xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

According to recent reports, "Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

It has been revealed that performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

Recent findings suggest that from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

Streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Recent findings suggest that latency also looks to be the major winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

Industry observers note that "Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

Of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Industry observers note that have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.
